title: How to Publish an RPG Maker MV Game on the Nintendo Switch Store?

posts.author: AravindStuddDeveloper
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I have a game made in
RPG Maker MV
, and I want to publish it on the
Nintendo eShop
for the
Nintendo Switch
. However, I have no idea how to do this.
I would appreciate any detailed guidance on the process, including:
Requirements:
What do I need to get started? (e.g., developer accounts, licenses, approvals)
Exporting:
How do I properly export an RPG Maker MV game for Switch?
Porting:
Do I need to convert the game into a different format? If so, how?
Kadokawa/Gotcha Gotcha Games:
Do they provide any official support for publishing RPG Maker games on Switch?
If anyone has
published an RPG Maker MV game on the Nintendo Switch before
, I would love to hear about your experience and any advice you can share.
Thanks in advance for any help!

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
I don't think it's that easy like that as RPG MV for PC/Mac/Linux
can only deploy to it.
Switch has RPG Maker on it to be build and shared (plugins cannot be used).
so if coding is required, it need to be build inside of it (no idea how much of
the core changes based on windows RPG MV core).
but there might be some 3rd party software to make it happen,  so it require
a couple of steps (easy or complex which I don't know).

posts.body:

Hi everyone,
I have a game made in

, and I want to publish it on the
Nintendo eShop
for the
Nintendo Switch
. However, I have no idea how to do this.
I would appreciate any detailed guidance on the process, including:
Requirements:
What do I need to get started? (e.g., developer accounts, licenses, approvals)
Exporting:
How do I properly export an RPG Maker MV game for Switch?
Porting:
Do I need to convert the game into a different format? If so, how?
Kadokawa/Gotcha Gotcha Games:
Do they provide any official support for publishing RPG Maker games on Switch?
Click to expand...
I've never tried to release on the Switch yet, but since I had other titles released, I am an authorized developer. To develop on the Switch or Switch 2, you need to go here:
https://developer.nintendo.com/
I've heard other developers getting denied because their design document, presentation, or demo did not meet Nintendo's standard. After two or three attempts, they were permitted. If I remember right, it took them less than 6 months to make the fixes, giving them more than enough time to release. Nintendo employees usually look for polish in graphics and programming. Nintendo also never does AO or 18+ games. Everyone instantly gets turned down for it. Nintendo is the family friendly system. Sometimes, they accept more controversial, but it should still be for each kind of family.
If you are an official Nintendo developer, you're not supposed to give much details about it because you must sign the non-disclosure agreement as soon as you're registered. They have a long list of compliance terms. Because of it, I'm not allowed to say too much.
After you sign-in, you will be presented with important news about the platforms and tools necessary to release your game. Some tools are free and others cost money depending on the device or platform.
In terms of a port, you would most likely need to do a port to C++. There are a couple of ways to do that. The first is a native port from the ground up. Eric Barone, Concerned Ape, the creator of Stardew Valley had to do ports of his game. Also, Markus Persson (Notch) had to do ports of Minecraft (PC to XBox). If you have time, he rewrote Minecraft in a
weekend in Java
. The other option is using a JS wrapper, which is often easier and quicker; however, it is less optimized. As long as you're not running probably hundreds or thousands of sprites at a time then it is usually alright. Every project is different and unexpected accidents show up everywhere in games and software. Most developers ignore optimization because the hardware is so powerful, but I like to optimize the system then add in more graphical details like layers or post-process effects.
